PERFORMANCE IMPROVEMENT PLAN

Employee: Dmitri Sokolov-Reyes
Position: Senior Account Manager, Central Region
Manager: Aisha Nkemdirim
HR Business Partner: Colm Brennan
Plan start date: May 11, 2026
Plan review dates: June 8, 2026 and July 6, 2026
Plan end date: August 3, 2026

PURPOSE

This plan sets out the specific performance concerns identified in your role, the standards you are expected to meet, the support the company will provide, and the timeline for review. Your employment remains at will, and nothing in this plan changes that or creates a contract of employment for any period.

PERFORMANCE CONCERNS

1. Pipeline accuracy. Forecast submissions for Q4 2025 and Q1 2026 overstated closed-won revenue by 38% and 41% respectively. Forecast accuracy for the region is expected to fall within 15%.

2. Account documentation. Fourteen of twenty-two active opportunities reviewed on April 28, 2026 had no contact activity logged in the CRM within the preceding thirty days, against a documented team standard of weekly logging.

3. Escalation handling. Three customer escalations in Q1 2026 were routed to the manager without a written summary or proposed resolution, contrary to the escalation procedure issued on September 3, 2025.

EXPECTED STANDARDS

By the plan end date you are expected to: submit forecasts within 15% accuracy for two consecutive months; log contact activity for every active opportunity at least weekly; and submit a written summary and proposed resolution with every escalation before routing it.

SUPPORT PROVIDED

The company will provide: weekly one-to-one coaching with the manager for the duration of the plan; a refresher session on the forecasting model with Revenue Operations in the week of May 18, 2026; and shadowing of two escalation handoffs with a senior peer.

REVIEW AND CONSEQUENCES

Progress will be reviewed at each review date and at the plan end date. Failure to meet the expected standards by the plan end date may result in further action up to and including termination of employment. Meeting the standards during the plan does not preclude further action if performance falls below the standard afterward.
